units.leftText: Now Solomon son of David established himself securely over his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and highly exalted him.
units.rightText: And Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom, and Jehovah his God was with him, and magnified him exceedingly.

units.leftText: Then Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel— the heads of the families.
units.rightText: And Solomon spake unto all Israel, to the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and to the judges, and to every prince in all Israel, the heads of the fathers’ houses.

units.leftText: And Solomon and the whole assembly went to the high place at Gibeon because it was the location of God’s Tent of Meeting, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness.
units.rightText: So Solomon, and all the assembly with him, went to the high place that was at Gibeon; for there was the tent of meeting of God, which Moses the servant of Jehovah had made in the wilderness.

units.leftText: Now David had brought the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, because he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: But the ark of God had David brought up from Kiriath-jearim to the place that David had prepared for it; for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem.

units.leftText: But the bronze altar made by Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, was in Gibeon before the tabernacle of the LORD. So Solomon and the assembly inquired of Him there.
units.rightText: Moreover the brazen altar, that Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made, was there before the tabernacle of Jehovah: and Solomon and the assembly sought unto it.
leftNotes: 1:5 LXX, Vulgate, and some Hebrew manuscripts was there before; MT he placed before

units.leftText: Solomon offered sacrifices there before the LORD on the bronze altar at the Tent of Meeting, where he offered a thousand burnt offerings.
units.rightText: And Solomon went up thither to the brazen altar before Jehovah, which was at the tent of meeting, and offered a thousand burnt-offerings upon it.

units.leftText: That night God appeared to Solomon and said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”
units.rightText: In that night did God appear unto Solomon, and said unto him, Ask what I shall give thee.

units.leftText: Solomon replied to God: “You have shown much loving devotion to my father David, and You have made me king in his place.
units.rightText: And Solomon said unto God, Thou hast showed great lovingkindness unto David my father, and hast made me king in his stead.
leftNotes: 1:8 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Now, O LORD God, let Your promise to my father David be fulfilled. For You have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
units.rightText: Now, O Jehovah God, let thy promise unto David my father be established; for thou hast made me king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude.

units.leftText: Now grant me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may lead this people. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”
units.rightText: Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this thy people, that is so great?
leftNotes: 1:10 Literally so that I may go out before this people and come in

units.leftText: God said to Solomon, “Since this was in your heart instead of requesting riches or wealth or honor for yourself or death for your enemies — and since you have not even requested long life but have asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern My people over whom I have made you king —
units.rightText: And God said to Solomon, Because this was in thy heart, and thou hast not asked riches, wealth, or honor, nor the life of them that hate thee, neither yet hast asked long life; but hast asked wisdom and knowledge for thyself, that thou mayest judge my people, over whom I have made thee king:

units.leftText: therefore wisdom and knowledge have been granted to you. And I will also give you riches and wealth and honor unlike anything given to the kings before you or after you.”
units.rightText: wisdom and knowledge is granted unto thee; and I will give thee riches, and wealth, and honor, such as none of the kings have had that have been before thee; neither shall there any after thee have the like.

units.leftText: So Solomon went to Jerusalem from the high place in Gibeon, from before the Tent of Meeting, and he reigned over Israel. Solomon’s Riches (1 Kings 10:26–29|1KI 10:26-29*)
units.rightText: So Solomon came from the high place that was at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, unto Jerusalem; and he reigned over Israel.

units.leftText: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he placed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 1:14 Literally Solomon accumulated chariots and horses; he had
1:14 Or horsemen or charioteers

units.leftText: The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
units.rightText: And the king made silver and gold to be in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he to be as the sycomore-trees that are in the lowland, for abundance.
leftNotes: 1:15 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.
units.rightText: And the horses which Solomon had were brought out of Egypt; the king’s merchants received them in droves, each drove at a price.
leftNotes: 1:16 Probably an area in Cilicia, a province in the southeast of Asia Minor

units.leftText: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
units.rightText: And they fetched up and brought out of Egypt a chariot for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty: and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and the kings of Syria, did they bring them out by their means.
leftNotes: 1:17 600 shekels is approximately 15.1 pounds or 6.8 kilograms of silver.
1:17 150 shekels is approximately 3.8 pounds or 1.7 kilograms of silver.

units.leftText: Now Solomon purposed to build a house for the Name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
units.rightText: Now Solomon purposed to build a house for the name of Jehovah, and a house for his kingdom.

units.leftText: So he conscripted 70,000 porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors.
units.rightText: And Solomon counted out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand men that were hewers in the mountains, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them.

units.leftText: Then Solomon sent word to Hiram king of Tyre:
units.rightText: And Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, As thou didst deal with David my father, and didst send him cedars to build him a house to dwell therein, even so deal with me.
leftNotes: 2:3 Hebrew Huram, a variant of Hiram; also in verses 11 and 12

units.leftText: Behold, I am about to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God to dedicate to Him for burning fragrant incense before Him, for displaying the showbread continuously, and for making burnt offerings every morning and evening as well as on the Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed feasts of the LORD our God. This is ordained for Israel forever.
units.rightText: Behold, I am about to build a house for the name of Jehovah my God, to dedicate it to him, and to burn before him incense of sweet spices, and for the continual showbread, and for the burnt-offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the set feasts of Jehovah our God. This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.

units.leftText: The house that I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
units.rightText: And the house which I build is great; for great is our God above all gods.

units.leftText: But who is able to build a house for Him, since the heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain Him? Who then am I, that I should build a house for Him, except as a place to burn sacrifices before Him?
units.rightText: But who is able to build him a house, seeing heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain him? who am I then, that I should build him a house, save only to burn incense before him?

units.leftText: Send me, therefore, a craftsman skilled in engraving to work with gold and silver, with bronze and iron, and with purple, crimson, and blue yarn. He will work with my craftsmen in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
units.rightText: Now therefore send me a man skilful to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass, and in iron, and in purple, and crimson, and blue, and that knoweth how to grave all manner of gravings, to be with the skilful men that are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father did provide.

units.leftText: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon, for I know that your servants have skill to cut timber there. And indeed, my servants will work with yours
units.rightText: Send me also cedar-trees, fir-trees, and algum-trees, out of Lebanon; for I know that thy servants know how to cut timber in Lebanon. And, behold, my servants shall be with thy servants,
leftNotes: 2:8 Or pine or juniper or fir
2:8 Algum is probably a variant of almug; see 1 Kings 10:11|1KI 10:11*.

units.leftText: to prepare for me timber in abundance, because the temple I am building will be great and wonderful.
units.rightText: even to prepare me timber in abundance; for the house which I am about to build shall be great and wonderful.

units.leftText: I will pay your servants, the woodcutters, 20,000 cors of ground wheat, 20,000 cors of barley, 20,000 baths of wine, and 20,000 baths of olive oil. ” Hiram’s Reply to Solomon (1 Kings 5:7–12|1KI 5:7-12*)
units.rightText: And, behold, I will give to thy servants, the hewers that cut timber, twenty thousand measures of beaten wheat, and twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.
leftNotes: 2:10 20,000 cors is approximately 124,800 bushels or 4.4 million liters (probably about 3,800 tons or 3,400 metric tons of wheat).
2:10 20,000 cors is approximately 124,800 bushels or 4.4 million liters (probably about 2,910 tons or 2,700 metric tons of barley).
2:10 20,000 baths is approximately 116,000 gallons or 440,000 liters of wine.
2:10 Or 20,000 baths of oil; that is, approximately 116,000 gallons or 440,000 liters

units.leftText: Then Hiram king of Tyre wrote a letter in reply to Solomon: “Because the LORD loves His people, He has set you over them as king.”
units.rightText: Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, Because Jehovah loveth his people, he hath made thee king over them.

units.leftText: And Hiram added: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth! He has given King David a wise son with insight and understanding, who will build a temple for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
units.rightText: Huram said moreover, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son, endued with discretion and understanding, that should build a house for Jehovah, and a house for his kingdom.

units.leftText: So now I am sending you Huram-abi, a skillful man endowed with creativity.
units.rightText: And now I have sent a skilful man, endued with understanding, of Huram my father’s,
leftNotes: 2:13 Or understanding

units.leftText: He is the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, and his father is a man of Tyre. He is skilled in work with gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple, blue, and crimson yarn, and fine linen. He is experienced in every kind of engraving and can execute any design that is given him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord, your father David.
units.rightText: the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan; and his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson, also to grave any manner of graving, and to devise any device; that there may be a place appointed unto him with thy skilful men, and with the skilful men of my lord David thy father.

units.leftText: Now let my lord send to his servants the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine he promised.
units.rightText: Now therefore the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine, which my lord hath spoken of, let him send unto his servants:

units.leftText: We will cut logs from Lebanon, as many as you need, and we will float them to you as rafts by sea down to Joppa. Then you can take them up to Jerusalem.”
units.rightText: and we will cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as thou shalt need; and we will bring it to thee in floats by sea to Joppa; and thou shalt carry it up to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Solomon numbered all the foreign men in the land of Israel following the census his father David had conducted, and there were found to be 153,600 in all.
units.rightText: And Solomon numbered all the sojourners that were in the land of Israel, after the numbering wherewith David his father had numbered them; and they were found a hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred.

units.leftText: Solomon made 70,000 of them porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors.
units.rightText: And he set threescore and ten thousand of them to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand that were hewers in the mountains, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to set the people at work.

units.leftText: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David. This was the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
units.rightText: Then Solomon began to build the house of Jehovah at Jerusalem on mount Moriah, where Jehovah appeared unto David his father, which he made ready in the place that David had appointed, in the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
leftNotes: 3:1 See LXX; Hebrew where He had appeared
3:1 Ornan is a variant of Araunah; see 2 Samuel 24:16|2SA 24:16*.

units.leftText: Solomon began construction on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
units.rightText: And he began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.

units.leftText: The foundation that Solomon laid for the house of God was sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, according to the old standard.
units.rightText: Now these are the foundations which Solomon laid for the building of the house of God. The length by cubits after the first measure was threescore cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits.
leftNotes: 3:3 The foundation was approximately 90 feet long and 30 feet wide (27.4 meters long and 9.1 meters wide).

3:3 The old standard of measurement was a cubit equal to 18 inches or 45.7 centimeters. The new standard, a cubit of approximately 21 inches or 53.3 centimeters (the long cubit) is the basic unit of length throughout Ezekiel 40 to 48.

units.leftText: The portico at the front, extending across the width of the temple, was twenty cubits long and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold. The Temple’s Interior (1 Kings 6:14–22|1KI 6:14-22*)
units.rightText: And the porch that was before the house, the length of it, according to the breadth of the house, was twenty cubits, and the height a hundred and twenty; and he overlaid it within with pure gold.
leftNotes: 3:4 20 cubits is approximately 30 feet or 9.1 meters; also in verses 8, 11, and 13.
3:4 Some LXX and Syriac manuscripts; Hebrew 120 cubits high (approximately 180 feet or 54.9 meters)

units.leftText: He paneled the main room with cypress, which he overlaid with fine gold and decorated with palm trees and chains.
units.rightText: And the greater house he ceiled with fir-wood, which he overlaid with fine gold, and wrought thereon palm-trees and chains.
leftNotes: 3:5 Or pine or juniper or fir

units.leftText: He adorned the temple with precious stones for beauty, and its gold was from Parvaim.
units.rightText: And he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty: and the gold was gold of Parvaim.

units.leftText: He overlaid its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
units.rightText: He overlaid also the house, the beams, the thresholds, and the walls thereof, and the doors thereof, with gold; and graved cherubim on the walls.

units.leftText: Then he made the Most Holy Place; its length corresponded to the width of the temple— twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. And he overlaid the inside with six hundred talents of fine gold.
units.rightText: And he made the most holy house: the length thereof, according to the breadth of the house, was twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents.
leftNotes: 3:8 Or the Holy of Holies; also in verse 10
3:8 600 talents is approximately 22.6 tons or 20.5 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold. The Cherubim (1 Kings 6:23–30|1KI 6:23-30*)
units.rightText: And the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.
leftNotes: 3:9 50 shekels is approximately 1.26 pounds or 569.8 grams of gold.

units.leftText: In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work, and he overlaid them with gold.
units.rightText: And in the most holy house he made two cherubim of image work; and they overlaid them with gold.

units.leftText: The total wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the wall of the temple, and its other wing was five cubits long and touched the wing of the other cherub.
units.rightText: And the wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long: the wing of the one cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing was likewise five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub.
leftNotes: 3:11 5 cubits is approximately 7.5 feet or 2.3 meters; also in verse 15.

units.leftText: The wing of the second cherub also measured five cubits and touched the wall of the temple, while its other wing measured five cubits and touched the wing of the first cherub.
units.rightText: And the wing of the other cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing was five cubits also, joining to the wing of the other cherub.

units.leftText: So the total wingspan of these cherubim was twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main room. The Veil and Pillars (1 Kings 7:13–22|1KI 7:13-22*)
units.rightText: The wings of these cherubim spread themselves forth twenty cubits: and they stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.

units.leftText: He made the veil of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it.
units.rightText: And he made the veil of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and wrought cherubim thereon.

units.leftText: In front of the temple he made two pillars, which together were thirty-five cubits high, each with a capital on top measuring five cubits.
units.rightText: Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty and five cubits high, and the capital that was on the top of each of them was five cubits.
leftNotes: 3:15 35 cubits is approximately 52.5 feet or 16 meters.

units.leftText: He made interwoven chains and put them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them into the chainwork.
units.rightText: And he made chains in the oracle, and put them on the tops of the pillars; and he made a hundred pomegranates, and put them on the chains.
leftNotes: 3:16 Or He made chains in the inner sanctuary

units.leftText: Then he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the south and one on the north. The pillar on the south he named Jachin, and the pillar on the north he named Boaz.
units.rightText: And he set up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand, and the other on the left; and called the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz.
leftNotes: 3:17 Jachin probably means He establishes.
3:17 Boaz probably means in Him is strength.

units.leftText: He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
units.rightText: Moreover he made an altar of brass, twenty cubits the length thereof, and twenty cubits the breadth thereof, and ten cubits the height thereof.
leftNotes: 4:1 The altar was approximately 30 feet in length and width and 15 feet high (9.1 meters in length and width and 4.6 meters high).

units.leftText: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
units.rightText: Also he made the molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim, round in compass; and the height thereof was five cubits; and a line of thirty cubits compassed it round about.
leftNotes: 4:2 The Sea was approximately 15 feet from rim to rim, 7.5 feet in height, and 45 feet in circumference (4.6 meters from rim to rim, 2.3 meters in height, and 13.7 meters in circumference).

units.leftText: Below the rim, figures of oxen encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.
units.rightText: And under it was the likeness of oxen, which did compass it round about, for ten cubits, compassing the sea round about. The oxen were in two rows, cast when it was cast.

units.leftText: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.
units.rightText: It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east: and the sea was set upon them above, and all their hinder parts were inward.

units.leftText: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold three thousand baths. The Ten Basins, Lampstands, and Tables (1 Kings 7:38–39|1KI 7:38-39*)
units.rightText: And it was a handbreadth thick; and the brim thereof was wrought like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily: it received and held three thousand baths.
leftNotes: 4:5 A handbreadth is approximately 2.9 inches or 7.4 centimeters.
4:5 3,000 baths is approximately 17,400 gallons or 66,000 liters.

units.leftText: He also made ten basins for washing and placed five on the south side and five on the north. The parts of the burnt offering were rinsed in them, but the priests used the Sea for washing.
units.rightText: He made also ten lavers, and put five on the right hand, and five on the left, to wash in them; such things as belonged to the burnt-offering they washed in them; but the sea was for the priests to wash in.

units.leftText: He made ten gold lampstands according to their specifications and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.
units.rightText: And he made the ten candlesticks of gold according to the ordinance concerning them; and he set them in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left.

units.leftText: Additionally, he made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. He also made a hundred gold bowls. The Courts
units.rightText: He made also ten tables, and placed them in the temple, five on the right side, and five on the left. And he made a hundred basins of gold.

units.leftText: He made the courtyard of the priests and the large court with its doors, and he overlaid the doors with bronze.
units.rightText: Furthermore he made the court of the priests, and the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid the doors of them with brass.

units.leftText: He put the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner. Completion of the Bronze Works (1 Kings 7:40–47|1KI 7:40-47*)
units.rightText: And he set the sea on the right side of the house eastward, toward the south.

units.leftText: Additionally, Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of God:
units.rightText: And Huram made the pots, and the shovels, and the basins. So Huram made an end of doing the work that he wrought for king Solomon in the house of God:

units.leftText: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars; the two sets of network covering both bowls of the capitals atop the pillars;
units.rightText: the two pillars, and the bowls, and the two capitals which were on the top of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars,

units.leftText: the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of network (two rows of pomegranates for each network covering both the bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars);
units.rightText: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks; two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the pillars.

units.leftText: the stands; the basins on the stands;
units.rightText: He made also the bases, and the lavers made he upon the bases;

units.leftText: the Sea; the twelve oxen underneath the Sea;
units.rightText: one sea, and the twelve oxen under it.

units.leftText: and the pots, shovels, meat forks, and all the other articles.
units.rightText: The pots also, and the shovels, and the flesh-hooks, and all the vessels thereof, did Huram his father make for king Solomon, for the house of Jehovah, of bright brass.

units.leftText: The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zeredah.
units.rightText: In the plain of the Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
leftNotes: 4:17 Zeredah is a variant of Zarethan; see 1 Kings 7:46|1KI 7:46*.

units.leftText: Solomon made all these articles in such great abundance that the weight of the bronze could not be determined. Completion of the Gold Furnishings (1 Kings 7:48–51|1KI 7:48-51*)
units.rightText: Thus Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance: for the weight of the brass could not be found out.

units.leftText: Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of God: the golden altar; the tables on which was placed the Bread of the Presence;
units.rightText: And Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of God, the golden altar also, and the tables whereon was the showbread;

units.leftText: the lampstands of pure gold and their lamps, to burn in front of the inner sanctuary as prescribed;
units.rightText: and the candlesticks with their lamps, to burn according to the ordinance before the oracle, of pure gold;

units.leftText: the flowers, lamps, and tongs of gold— of purest gold;
units.rightText: and the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs, of gold, and that perfect gold;

units.leftText: the wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, and censers of pure gold; and the gold doors of the temple: the inner doors to the Most Holy Place as well as the doors of the main hall.
units.rightText: and the snuffers, and the basins, and the spoons, and the firepans, of pure gold. And as for the entry of the house, the inner doors thereof for the most holy place, and the doors of the house, to wit, of the temple, were of gold.
leftNotes: 4:22 Or the Holy of Holies

units.leftText: So all the work that Solomon had performed for the house of the LORD was completed. Then Solomon brought in the items his father David had dedicated— the silver, the gold, and all the furnishings— and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of God.
units.rightText: Thus all the work that Solomon wrought for the house of Jehovah was finished. And Solomon brought in the things that David his father had dedicated, even the silver, and the gold, and all the vessels, and put them in the treasuries of the house of God.

units.leftText: At that time Solomon assembled in Jerusalem the elders of Israel— all the tribal heads and family leaders of the Israelites — to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David.
units.rightText: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers’ houses of the children of Israel, unto Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of the city of David, which is Zion.

units.leftText: So all the men of Israel came together to the king at the feast in the seventh month.
units.rightText: And all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto the king at the feast, which was in the seventh month.
leftNotes: 5:3 That is, the Feast of Tabernacles (or Booths or Shelters); see Leviticus 23:33–36|LEV 23:33-36*.

units.leftText: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites took up the ark,
units.rightText: And all the elders of Israel came: and the Levites took up the ark;

units.leftText: and they brought up the ark and the Tent of Meeting with all its sacred furnishings. The Levitical priests carried them up.
units.rightText: and they brought up the ark, and the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the Tent; these did the priests the Levites bring up.

units.leftText: There, before the ark, King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had assembled with him sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
units.rightText: And king Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, that were assembled unto him, were before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be counted nor numbered for multitude.

units.leftText: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
units.rightText: And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of Jehovah unto its place, into the oracle of the house, to the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubim.
leftNotes: 5:7 Or the Holy of Holies

units.leftText: For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadowed the ark and its poles.
units.rightText: For the cherubim spread forth their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and the staves thereof above.

units.leftText: The poles of the ark extended far enough that their ends were visible from in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place; and they are there to this day.
units.rightText: And the staves were so long that the ends of the staves were seen from the ark before the oracle; but they were not seen without: and there it is unto this day.
leftNotes: 5:9 Some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX The poles extended far enough that their ends were visible from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary; see 1 Kings 8:8|1KI 8:8*.
5:9 Literally not from outside

units.leftText: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites after they had come out of Egypt.
units.rightText: There was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put there at Horeb, when Jehovah made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of Egypt.
leftNotes: 5:10 That is, Mount Sinai, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai

units.leftText: Now all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves regardless of their divisions. And when the priests came out of the Holy Place,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place (for all the priests that were present had sanctified themselves, and did not keep their courses;

units.leftText: all the Levitical singers — Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives — stood on the east side of the altar, dressed in fine linen and playing cymbals, harps, and lyres, accompanied by 120 priests sounding trumpets.
units.rightText: also the Levites who were the singers, all of them, even Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and their brethren, arrayed in fine linen, with cymbals and psalteries and harps, stood at the east end of the altar, and with them a hundred and twenty priests sounding with trumpets);

units.leftText: The trumpeters and singers joined together to praise and thank the LORD with one voice. They lifted up their voices, accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, in praise to the LORD: “For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.”
units.rightText: it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking Jehovah; and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised Jehovah, saying, For he is good; for his lovingkindness endureth for ever; that then the house was filled with a cloud, even the house of Jehovah,

units.leftText: so that the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud. For the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
units.rightText: so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud: for the glory of Jehovah filled the house of God.

units.leftText: Then Solomon declared: “The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.
units.rightText: Then spake Solomon, Jehovah hath said that he would dwell in the thick darkness.

units.leftText: But I have built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.”
units.rightText: But I have built thee a house of habitation, and a place for thee to dwell in for ever.

units.leftText: And as the whole assembly of Israel stood there, the king turned around and blessed them all
units.rightText: And the king turned his face, and blessed all the assembly of Israel: and all the assembly of Israel stood.

units.leftText: and said:
units.rightText: And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, who spake with his mouth unto David my father, and hath with his hands fulfilled it, saying,

units.leftText: ‘Since the day I brought My people out of the land of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel in which to build a house so that My Name would be there, nor have I chosen anyone to be ruler over My people Israel.
units.rightText: Since the day that I brought forth my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house in, that my name might be there; neither chose I any man to be prince over my people Israel:

units.leftText: But now I have chosen Jerusalem for My Name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.’
units.rightText: but I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there, and have chosen David to be over my people Israel.

units.leftText: Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to my father David, ‘Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well to have this in your heart.
units.rightText: But Jehovah said unto David my father, Whereas it was in thy heart to build a house for my name, thou didst well that it was in thy heart:

units.leftText: Nevertheless, you are not the one to build it; but your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name.’
units.rightText: nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house for my name.

units.leftText: Now the LORD has fulfilled the word that He spoke. I have succeeded my father David, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: And Jehovah hath performed his word that he spake; for I am risen up in the room of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as Jehovah promised, and have built the house for the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: And there I have placed the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that He made with the children of Israel.” Solomon’s Prayer of Dedication (1 Kings 8:22–53|1KI 8:22-53*)
units.rightText: And there have I set the ark, wherein is the covenant of Jehovah, which he made with the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.
units.rightText: And he stood before the altar of Jehovah in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread forth his hands

units.leftText: Now Solomon had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high and had placed it in the middle of the courtyard. He stood on it, knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,
units.rightText: (for Solomon had made a brazen scaffold, five cubits long, and five cubits broad, and three cubits high, and had set it in the midst of the court; and upon it he stood, and kneeled down upon his knees before all the assembly of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven);
leftNotes: 6:13 The platform was approximately 7.5 feet in length and width, and 4.5 feet high (2.3 meters in length and width, and 1.4 meters high).

units.leftText: and said:
units.rightText: and he said, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, there is no God like thee, in heaven, or on earth; who keepest covenant and lovingkindness with thy servants, that walk before thee with all their heart;

units.leftText: You have kept Your promise to Your servant, my father David. What You spoke with Your mouth You have fulfilled with Your hand this day.
units.rightText: who hast kept with thy servant David my father that which thou didst promise him: yea, thou spakest with thy mouth, and hast fulfilled it with thy hand, as it is this day.

units.leftText: Therefore now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant, my father David, what You promised when You said: ‘You will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants guard their way to walk in My law as you have walked before Me.’
units.rightText: Now therefore, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, keep with thy servant David my father that which thou hast promised him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel, if only thy children take heed to their way, to walk in my law as thou hast walked before me.

units.leftText: And now, O LORD, God of Israel, please confirm what You promised to Your servant David.
units.rightText: Now therefore, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, let thy word be verified, which thou spakest unto thy servant David.

units.leftText: But will God indeed dwell with man upon the earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.
units.rightText: But will God in very deed dwell with men on the earth? behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house which I have builded!

units.leftText: Yet regard the prayer and plea of Your servant, O LORD my God, so that You may hear the cry and the prayer that Your servant is praying before You.
units.rightText: Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O Jehovah my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer which thy servant prayeth before thee;

units.leftText: May Your eyes be open toward this temple day and night, toward the place where You said You would put Your Name, so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
units.rightText: that thine eyes may be open toward this house day and night, even toward the place whereof thou hast said that thou wouldest put thy name there; to hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall pray toward this place.

units.leftText: Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. May You hear and forgive.
units.rightText: And hearken thou to the supplications of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, when they shall pray toward this place: yea, hear thou from thy dwelling-place, even from heaven; and when thou hearest, forgive.

units.leftText: When a man sins against his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes to take an oath before Your altar in this temple,
units.rightText: If a man sin against his neighbor, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to swear, and he come and swear before thine altar in this house;

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven and act. May You judge Your servants, condemning the wicked man by bringing down on his own head what he has done, and justifying the righteous man by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
units.rightText: then hear thou from heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, requiting the wicked, to bring his way upon his own head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.

units.leftText: When Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and confess Your name, praying and pleading before You in this temple,
units.rightText: And if thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again and confess thy name, and pray and make supplication before thee in this house;

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel. May You restore them to the land You gave to them and their fathers.
units.rightText: then hear thou from heaven, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest to them and to their fathers.

units.leftText: When the skies are shut and there is no rain because Your people have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and they turn from their sins because You have afflicted them,
units.rightText: When the heavens are shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; if they pray toward this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou dost afflict them:

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel, so that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk. May You send rain on the land that You gave Your people as an inheritance.
units.rightText: then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants, and of thy people Israel, when thou teachest them the good way wherein they should walk; and send rain upon thy land, which thou hast given to thy people for an inheritance.

units.leftText: When famine or plague comes upon the land, or blight or mildew or locusts or grasshoppers, or when their enemies besiege them in their cities, whatever plague or sickness may come,
units.rightText: If there be in the land famine, if there be pestilence, if there be blasting or mildew, locust or caterpillar; if their enemies besiege them in the land of their cities; whatsoever plague or whatsoever sickness there be;

units.leftText: then may whatever prayer or plea Your people Israel make— each knowing his own afflictions and spreading out his hands toward this temple—
units.rightText: what prayer and supplication soever be made by any man, or by all thy people Israel, who shall know every man his own plague and his own sorrow, and shall spread forth his hands toward this house:

units.leftText: be heard by You from heaven, Your dwelling place. And may You forgive and repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart — for You alone know the hearts of men —
units.rightText: then hear thou from heaven thy dwelling-place, and forgive, and render unto every man according to all his ways, whose heart thou knowest (for thou, even thou only, knowest the hearts of the children of men);

units.leftText: so that they may fear You and walk in Your ways all the days they live in the land that You gave to our fathers.
units.rightText: that they may fear thee, to walk in thy ways, so long as they live in the land which thou gavest unto our fathers.

units.leftText: And as for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of Your great name and Your mighty hand and outstretched arm — when he comes and prays toward this temple,
units.rightText: Moreover concerning the foreigner, that is not of thy people Israel, when he shall come from a far country for thy great name’s sake, and thy mighty hand, and thine outstretched arm; when they shall come and pray toward this house:

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You. Then all the peoples of the earth will know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and they will know that this house I have built is called by Your Name.
units.rightText: then hear thou from heaven, even from thy dwelling-place, and do according to all that the foreigner calleth to thee for; that all the peoples of the earth may know thy name, and fear thee, as doth thy people Israel, and that they may know that this house which I have built is called by thy name.

units.leftText: When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and when they pray to You in the direction of this city You have chosen and the house I have built for Your Name,
units.rightText: If thy people go out to battle against their enemies, by whatsoever way thou shalt send them, and they pray unto thee toward this city which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy name;

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.
units.rightText: then hear thou from heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

units.leftText: When they sin against You— for there is no one who does not sin— and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them as captives to a land far or near,
units.rightText: If they sin against thee (for there is no man that sinneth not), and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captive unto a land far off or near;

units.leftText: and when they come to their senses in the land to which they were taken, and they repent and plead with You in the land of their captors, saying, ‘We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly,’
units.rightText: yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they are carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication unto thee in the land of their captivity, saying, We have sinned, we have done perversely, and have dealt wickedly;

units.leftText: and when they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of the enemies who took them captive, and when they pray in the direction of the land that You gave to their fathers, the city You have chosen, and the house I have built for Your Name,
units.rightText: if they return unto thee with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity, whither they have carried them captive, and pray toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers, and the city which thou hast chosen, and toward the house which I have built for thy name:

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, their prayer and pleas, and may You uphold their cause. May You forgive Your people who sinned against You.
units.rightText: then hear thou from heaven, even from thy dwelling-place, their prayer and their supplications, and maintain their cause, and forgive thy people who have sinned against thee.

units.leftText: Now, my God, may Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.
units.rightText: Now, O my God, let, I beseech thee, thine eyes be open, and let thine ears be attent, unto the prayer that is made in this place.

units.leftText: Now therefore, arise, O LORD God, and enter Your resting place, You and the ark of Your might. May Your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may Your godly ones rejoice in goodness.
units.rightText: Now therefore arise, O Jehovah God, into thy resting-place, thou, and the ark of thy strength: let thy priests, O Jehovah God, be clothed with salvation, and let thy saints rejoice in goodness.

units.leftText: O LORD God, do not reject Your anointed one. Remember Your loving devotion to Your servant David.”
units.rightText: O Jehovah God, turn not away the face of thine anointed: remember thy lovingkindnesses to David thy servant.

units.leftText: When Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
units.rightText: Now when Solomon had made an end of praying, the fire came down from heaven, and consumed the burnt-offering and the sacrifices; and the glory of Jehovah filled the house.

units.leftText: The priests were unable to enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled it.
units.rightText: And the priests could not enter into the house of Jehovah, because the glory of Jehovah filled Jehovah’s house.

units.leftText: When all the Israelites saw the fire coming down and the glory of the LORD above the temple, they bowed down on the pavement with their faces to the ground, and they worshiped and gave thanks to the LORD: “For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.” Sacrifices of Dedication (1 Kings 8:62–66|1KI 8:62-66*)
units.rightText: And all the children of Israel looked on, when the fire came down, and the glory of Jehovah was upon the house; and they bowed themselves with their faces to the ground upon the pavement, and worshipped, and gave thanks unto Jehovah, saying, For he is good; for his lovingkindness endureth for ever.

units.leftText: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
units.rightText: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifice before Jehovah.

units.leftText: And King Solomon offered a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.
units.rightText: And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty and two thousand oxen, and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

units.leftText: The priests stood at their posts, as did the Levites with the musical instruments of the LORD, which King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD and with which David had offered praise, saying, “For His loving devotion endures forever.” Across from the Levites, the priests sounded trumpets, and all the Israelites were standing.
units.rightText: And the priests stood, according to their offices; the Levites also with instruments of music of Jehovah, which David the king had made to give thanks unto Jehovah (for his lovingkindness endureth for ever), when David praised by their ministry: and the priests sounded trumpets before them; and all Israel stood.

units.leftText: Then Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, and there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, since the bronze altar he had made could not hold all these offerings.
units.rightText: Moreover Solomon hallowed the middle of the court that was before the house of Jehovah; for there he offered the burnt-offerings, and the fat of the peace-offerings, because the brazen altar which Solomon had made was not able to receive the burnt-offering, and the meal-offering, and the fat.

units.leftText: So at that time Solomon and all Israel with him— a very great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt— kept the feast for seven days.
units.rightText: So Solomon held the feast at that time seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath unto the brook of Egypt.
leftNotes: 7:8 That is, the Feast of Tabernacles (or Booths or Shelters); see Leviticus 23:33–36|LEV 23:33-36*.

units.leftText: On the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for the dedication of the altar had lasted seven days, and the feast seven days more.
units.rightText: And on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly: for they kept the dedication of the altar seven days, and the feast seven days.

units.leftText: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people away to their homes, joyful and glad of heart for the good things that the LORD had done for David, for Solomon, and for His people Israel. The LORD’s Response to Solomon (1 Kings 9:1–9|1KI 9:1-9*)
units.rightText: And on the three and twentieth day of the seventh month he sent the people away unto their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the goodness that Jehovah had showed unto David, and to Solomon, and to Israel his people.

units.leftText: When Solomon had finished the house of the LORD and the royal palace, successfully carrying out all that was in his heart to do for the house of the LORD and for his own palace,
units.rightText: Thus Solomon finished the house of Jehovah, and the king’s house: and all that came into Solomon’s heart to make in the house of Jehovah, and in his own house, he prosperously effected.

units.leftText: the LORD appeared to him at night and said to him:
units.rightText: And Jehovah appeared to Solomon by night, and said unto him, I have heard thy prayer, and have chosen this place to myself for a house of sacrifice.

units.leftText: If I close the sky so there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send a plague among My people,
units.rightText: If I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people;

units.leftText: and if My people who are called by My name humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
units.rightText: if my people, who are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

units.leftText: Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
units.rightText: Now mine eyes shall be open, and mine ears attent, unto the prayer that is made in this place.

units.leftText: For I have now chosen and consecrated this temple so that My Name may be there forever. My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.
units.rightText: For now have I chosen and hallowed this house, that my name may be there for ever; and mine eyes and my heart shall be there perpetually.

units.leftText: And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, doing all I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and ordinances,
units.rightText: And as for thee, if thou wilt walk before me as David thy father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded thee, and wilt keep my statutes and mine ordinances;

units.leftText: then I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with your father David when I said, ‘You will never fail to have a man to rule over Israel.’
units.rightText: then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom, according as I covenanted with David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man to be ruler in Israel.

units.leftText: But if you turn away and forsake the statutes and commandments I have set before you, and if you go off to serve and worship other gods,
units.rightText: But if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments which I have set before you, and shall go and serve other gods, and worship them;

units.leftText: then I will uproot Israel from the soil I have given them, and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name. I will make it an object of scorn and ridicule among all the peoples.
units.rightText: then will I pluck them up by the roots out of my land which I have given them; and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight, and I will make it a proverb and a byword among all peoples.

units.leftText: And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’
units.rightText: And this house, which is so high, every one that passeth by it shall be astonished, and shall say, Why hath Jehovah done thus unto this land, and to this house?
leftNotes: 7:21 Some LXX manuscripts, Syriac, and Arabic; Hebrew And though this temple is now exalted; see also 1 Kings 9:8|1KI 9:8*.

units.leftText: And others will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them— because of this, He has brought all this disaster upon them.’”
units.rightText: And they shall answer, Because they forsook Jehovah, the God of their fathers, who brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods, and worshipped them, and served them: therefore hath he brought all this evil upon them.

units.leftText: Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own palace,
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, wherein Solomon had built the house of Jehovah, and his own house,

units.leftText: Solomon rebuilt the cities Hiram had given him and settled Israelites there.
units.rightText: that the cities which Huram had given to Solomon, Solomon built them, and caused the children of Israel to dwell there.
leftNotes: 8:2 Hebrew Huram, a variant of Hiram; also in verse 18

units.leftText: Then Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and captured it.
units.rightText: And Solomon went to Hamath-zobah, and prevailed against it.

units.leftText: He built Tadmor in the wilderness, in addition to all the store cities that he had built in Hamath.
units.rightText: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the store-cities, which he built in Hamath.

units.leftText: He rebuilt Upper and Lower Beth-horon as fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars,
units.rightText: Also he built Beth-horon the upper, and Beth-horon the nether, fortified cities, with walls, gates, and bars;

units.leftText: as well as Baalath, all the store cities that belonged to Solomon, and all the cities for his chariots and horses — whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout the land of his dominion.
units.rightText: and Baalath, and all the store-cities that Solomon had, and all the cities for his chariots, and the cities for his horsemen, and all that Solomon desired to build for his pleasure in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
leftNotes: 8:6 Or horsemen or charioteers

units.leftText: As for all the people who remained of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites (these people were not Israelites) —
units.rightText: As for all the people that were left of the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, that were not of Israel;

units.leftText: their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites had not destroyed — Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.
units.rightText: of their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel consumed not, of them did Solomon raise a levy of bondservants unto this day.

units.leftText: But Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slave labor, because they were his men of war, the leaders of his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
units.rightText: But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no servants for his work; but they were men of war, and chief of his captains, and rulers of his chariots and of his horsemen.

units.leftText: They were also the chief officers for King Solomon: 250 supervisors.
units.rightText: And these were the chief officers of king Solomon, even two hundred and fifty, that bare rule over the people.

units.leftText: Solomon brought the daughter of Pharaoh up from the City of David to the palace he had built for her. For he said, “My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy.”
units.rightText: And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh out of the city of David unto the house that he had built for her; for he said, My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because the places are holy, whereunto the ark of Jehovah hath come.

units.leftText: At that time Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD he had built in front of the portico.
units.rightText: Then Solomon offered burnt-offerings unto Jehovah on the altar of Jehovah, which he had built before the porch,

units.leftText: He observed the daily requirement for offerings according to the commandment of Moses for Sabbaths, New Moons, and the three annual appointed feasts — the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles.
units.rightText: even as the duty of every day required, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the set feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.
leftNotes: 8:13 That is, the seven-day period after the Passover during which no leaven may be eaten; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.
8:13 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Harvest(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16*) or the Feast of Pentecost(see Acts 2:1|ACT 2:1*).

8:13 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; also translated as the Feast of Booths or the Feast of Shelters and originally called the Feast of Ingathering(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16* and Exodus 34:22).

units.leftText: In keeping with the ordinances of his father David, Solomon appointed the divisions of the priests over their service, and the Levites for their duties to offer praise and to minister before the priests according to the daily requirement. He also appointed gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate, for this had been the command of David, the man of God.
units.rightText: And he appointed, according to the ordinance of David his father, the courses of the priests to their service, and the Levites to their offices, to praise, and to minister before the priests, as the duty of every day required; the doorkeepers also by their courses at every gate: for so had David the man of God commanded.

units.leftText: They did not turn aside from the king’s command regarding the priests or the Levites in any matter, including that of the treasuries.
units.rightText: And they departed not from the commandment of the king unto the priests and Levites concerning any matter, or concerning the treasures.

units.leftText: Thus all the work of Solomon was carried out, from the day the foundation was laid for the house of the LORD until it was finished. So the house of the LORD was completed.
units.rightText: Now all the work of Solomon was prepared unto the day of the foundation of the house of Jehovah, and until it was finished. So the house of Jehovah was completed.

units.leftText: Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth on the coast of Edom.
units.rightText: Then went Solomon to Ezion-geber, and to Eloth, on the sea-shore in the land of Edom.
leftNotes: 8:17 Eloth is a variant of Elath; see LXX, 2 Kings 14:22|2KI 14:22*, and 2 Kings 16:6.
8:17 That is, along the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Edom

units.leftText: So Hiram sent him ships captained by his servants, along with crews of experienced sailors. They went with Solomon’s servants to Ophir and acquired from there 450 talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.
units.rightText: And Huram sent him by the hands of his servants ships, and servants that had knowledge of the sea; and they came with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and fetched from thence four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and brought them to king Solomon.
leftNotes: 8:18 450 talents is approximately 17 tons or 15.4 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon, she came to test him with difficult questions. She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan— with camels bearing spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones.
units.rightText: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great train, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.

units.leftText: And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for him to explain.
units.rightText: And Solomon told her all her questions; and there was not anything hid from Solomon which he told her not.

units.leftText: When the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built,
units.rightText: And when the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

units.leftText: the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants, the attire of his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.
units.rightText: and the food of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, his cupbearers also, and their apparel, and his ascent by which he went up unto the house of Jehovah; there was no more spirit in her.
leftNotes: 9:4 LXX and Syriac (see also 1 Kings 10:5|1KI 10:5*); Hebrew and his stairway by which he went up

units.leftText: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true.
units.rightText: And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thine acts, and of thy wisdom.
leftNotes: 9:5 Or your achievements

units.leftText: But I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not half of the greatness of your wisdom was told to me. You have far exceeded the report I heard.
units.rightText: Howbeit I believed not their words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it; and, behold, the half of the greatness of thy wisdom was not told me: thou exceedest the fame that I heard.

units.leftText: How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
units.rightText: Happy are thy men, and happy are these thy servants, that stand continually before thee, and hear thy wisdom.

units.leftText: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on His throne to be king for the LORD your God. Because your God loved Israel enough to establish them forever, He has made you king over them to carry out justice and righteousness.”
units.rightText: Blessed be Jehovah thy God, who delighted in thee, to set thee on his throne, to be king for Jehovah thy God: because thy God loved Israel, to establish them for ever, therefore made he thee king over them, to do justice and righteousness.

units.leftText: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. There had never been such spices as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
units.rightText: And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great abundance, and precious stones: neither was there any such spice as the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.
leftNotes: 9:9 120 talents is approximately 4.52 tons or 4.1 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: (The servants of Hiram and of Solomon who brought gold from Ophir also brought algum wood and precious stones.
units.rightText: And the servants also of Huram, and the servants of Solomon, that brought gold from Ophir, brought algum-trees and precious stones.
leftNotes: 9:10 Algum is probably a variant of almug; also in verse 11; see 1 Kings 10:11|1KI 10:11*.

units.leftText: The king made the algum wood into steps for the house of the LORD and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had anything like them been seen in the land of Judah.)
units.rightText: And the king made of the algum-trees terraces for the house of Jehovah, and for the king’s house, and harps and psalteries for the singers: and there were none such seen before in the land of Judah.
leftNotes: 9:11 Or gateways

units.leftText: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired — whatever she asked — far more than she had brought the king. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants. Solomon’s Wealth and Splendor (1 Kings 10:14–29|1KI 10:14-29*)
units.rightText: And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, besides that which she had brought unto the king. So she turned, and went to her own land, she and her servants.

units.leftText: The weight of gold that came to Solomon each year was 666 talents,
units.rightText: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and threescore and six talents of gold,
leftNotes: 9:13 666 talents is approximately 25.1 tons or 22.8 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: not including the revenue from the merchants and traders. And all the Arabian kings and governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.
units.rightText: besides that which the traders and merchants brought: and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the country brought gold and silver to Solomon.

units.leftText: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of hammered gold went into each shield.
units.rightText: And king Solomon made two hundred bucklers of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of beaten gold went to one buckler.
leftNotes: 9:15 600 shekels is approximately 15.1 pounds or 6.8 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three hundred shekels of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
units.rightText: And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three hundred shekels of gold went to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
leftNotes: 9:16 300 shekels is approximately 7.5 pounds or 3.4 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
units.rightText: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold.

units.leftText: The throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold was attached to it. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.
units.rightText: And there were six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne, and stays on either side by the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the stays.

units.leftText: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.
units.rightText: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.

units.leftText: All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.
units.rightText: And all king Solomon’s drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold: silver was nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon.

units.leftText: For the king had the ships of Tarshish that went with Hiram’s servants, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
units.rightText: For the king had ships that went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram; once every three years came the ships of Tarshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
leftNotes: 9:21 Or a fleet of trading ships; twice in this verse
9:21 Hebrew Huram’s, a variant of Hiram’s
9:21 Or baboons

units.leftText: So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
units.rightText: So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

units.leftText: All the kings of the earth sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.
units.rightText: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

units.leftText: Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
units.rightText: And they brought every man his tribute, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and raiment, armor, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.

units.leftText: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots, and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 9:25 Or horsemen or charioteers

units.leftText: He reigned over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt.
units.rightText: And he ruled over all the kings from the River even unto the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt.
leftNotes: 9:26 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
units.rightText: And the king made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he to be as the sycomore-trees that are in the lowland, for abundance.
leftNotes: 9:27 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and from all the lands. The Death of Solomon (1 Kings 11:41–43|1KI 11:41-43*)
units.rightText: And they brought horses for Solomon out of Egypt, and out of all lands.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Solomon, from beginning to end, are they not written in the Records of Nathan the Prophet, in the Prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the Visions of Iddo the Seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
units.rightText: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat?

units.leftText: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
units.rightText: And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

units.leftText: And Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.
units.rightText: And Rehoboam went to Shechem; for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.

units.leftText: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he returned from Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it (for he was in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of king Solomon), that Jeroboam returned out of Egypt.

units.leftText: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and all Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
units.rightText: And they sent and called him; and Jeroboam and all Israel came, and they spake to Rehoboam, saying,

units.leftText: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you must lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
units.rightText: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee.

units.leftText: Rehoboam answered, “Come back to me in three days.” So the people departed.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Come again unto me after three days. And the people departed.

units.leftText: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
units.rightText: And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men, that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, What counsel give ye me to return answer to this people?

units.leftText: They replied, “If you will be kind to these people and please them by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
units.rightText: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.

units.leftText: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
units.rightText: But he forsook the counsel of the old men which they had given him, and took counsel with the young men that were grown up with him, that stood before him.

units.leftText: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’ ?”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, What counsel give ye, that we may return answer to this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke that thy father did put upon us lighter?

units.leftText: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
